output.market_context: This quarter's tracked filings cluster around semiconductors and power, with several managers opening large new positions rather than trimming existing ones. Insider confirmation is mixed: some names pair institutional accumulation with open-market purchases, while others show meaningful discretionary selling.

stocks.insider_read: A single officer/director open-market purchase of $9,999,985 with no reported sales gives unusually direct confirmation of the 13F signal.
risks: Filings lag up to 45 days; the -31% move since quarter-end may reflect news the filers have already acted on
One large insider purchase is a single data point, not a pattern
No prior build quarters, so accumulation is unproven
stocks.why_strongest: Four filers increased their reported long positions, including two new entries, one of which is sized at 8.3% of that manager's book, a top-decile weight. Concentration and consensus scores are both high, and the name is lightly held across the tracked group. Price is well below the quarter-end level, so entry conditions differ materially from the filers'.

stocks.insider_read: Insiders were net sellers: $27,599,960 sold across 39 trades against $1,544,981 of purchases by one officer/director, which does not confirm the 13F signal.
risks: Heavy insider selling directly contradicts the institutional accumulation
Price is up since quarter-end, so filers hold a better basis
The 30.3% weight reflects one highly concentrated manager, not broad sizing
stocks.why_strongest: Five independent managers increased reported long positions, with adds of several hundred percent and one filer holding 30.3% of its book in the name, a top-three portfolio weight. Consensus and conviction factors are near maximum with low crowding across the tracked group.

stocks.insider_read: An officer/director bought $1,173,069 across three open-market trades with no reported sales, a modest but clean confirmation.
risks: Two of the three buyers made small percentage adds; conviction is driven by one concentrated new entry
No prior build quarters
Utility and power demand narratives are widely traded and can reverse quickly
stocks.why_strongest: Three filers increased reported long positions, including a new position at 14.1% of that manager's book and an add from a high-quality buyer. Conviction and activity factors are at maximum, and the filing is relatively fresh.

stocks.insider_read: Purchases of $205,008 across three trades by one officer/director with no reported sales; small in absolute terms, so only weak confirmation.
risks: Most adds were marginal increases, not fresh conviction
Crowding is moderate, the only name in this list not labelled low
Insider purchase size is immaterial relative to the company
stocks.why_strongest: Six filers increased reported long positions, several of them long-horizon, high-quality managers with portfolio weights of 15% to 24%. Manager quality and consensus are the highest in this group, though most adds were small percentage increments to already-large holdings.

stocks.insider_read: Two insiders bought $251,113 across 22 open-market trades with no reported sales, a small-value but consistent pattern.
risks: Insider purchase value is small and may reflect routine plan-adjacent activity
One buyer is a quant filer with zero quality weighting
Price is 10% below the quarter-end level
stocks.why_strongest: Six independent filers increased reported long positions, including a new entry at 6.4% of that manager's book and a 10.5% weight from the largest holder. Breadth of buyers is the notable feature here rather than any single outsized position.

stocks.insider_read: One officer/director purchased $2,015,342 across three trades against $30,678 of sales in one trade, leaving a clearly net-buying stance.
risks: Only two buyers, and one made a marginal add; consensus is weak
Price fell 21% since quarter-end, so insider buying may be a drawdown response
No listed option met the liquidity and delta screens
stocks.why_strongest: The insider factor is the highest in the top ten and drives the score. A new position at 3.1% of one manager's book plus a small add from a value manager gives only narrow institutional support, but the two signals align.

stocks.insider_read: An officer/director bought $1,001,510 in one trade against $263,256 of sales in one trade, leaving a net-buying stance.
risks: A single buyer means no independent confirmation across filers
Consensus and activity factors are the weakest in the top ten
Price is down 20% since quarter-end
stocks.why_strongest: This is the accumulation case: two prior build quarters from a single high-quality, low-turnover manager now holding 10.6% of its book. Breadth is minimal, so the signal rests on persistence and manager quality rather than on consensus.

stocks.insider_read: Insiders were net sellers: $3,720,116 in one sale against $1,642,200 of purchases by two officers/directors, so the 13F signal is not confirmed.
risks: A single large sale outweighs the purchases
Price is 33% below the quarter-end level at which filers bought
No listed option cleared the volatility and liquidity screens
stocks.why_strongest: Three independent managers increased reported long positions, two of them opening new stakes and one lifting its holding to 6.4% of its book. Activity is high, but the name ranks here on institutional breadth alone.

stocks.insider_read: One officer/director purchased $100,181 with no reported sales, a token amount that offers only marginal confirmation.
risks: Single buyer, lowest consensus score in the group
Insider purchase value is very small
Price down 18% since quarter-end may reflect deteriorating fundamentals
stocks.why_strongest: Like ALK, this rests on persistence rather than breadth: two prior build quarters from one high-quality manager now at 11.0% of its book, with a fresh filing from a low-turnover holder. Consensus is very weak.

stocks.insider_read: No insider confirmation exists: purchases were $0, while insiders sold $37,056,411 across nine trades.
risks: Sizeable insider selling with no offsetting purchases
Price is up 10% since quarter-end, eroding the filers' entry advantage
Several adds were near-zero percentage changes to existing large holdings
stocks.why_strongest: Six filers increased reported long positions, including a new stake at 5.8% of one book and a 19.8% weight from a high-quality concentrated manager. Institutional consensus is strong, but the insider factor scores zero, which caps the overall signal.
